method.unit: round containing at least one of the twenty funds
method.null: degree-preserving edge-swap permutation, restricted to rounds in the same calendar year; every fund keeps its round count, every round keeps its number of these twenty funds, and activity windows are held
method.lift: observed shared rounds / mean shared rounds across permutations; 1.0 is chance
method.significance: empirical p from the permutations, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at 0.05
method.why_not_independence: Independence expects (rounds_a x rounds_b)/N, under which the median pair scores 0.55 — the model over-predicts co-investment for nearly every pair, because most rounds hold only one of these funds. The permutation null centres the median at 0.89.
method.caveat: Co-occurrence is not collaboration. Two funds in one cap table may never have spoken, and a low score can reflect stage, sector or geography rather than any decision to stay apart.
